title: Curvature criterion for lifting first-order formal projective-metrizability jets to second order
author: Ioan Bucataru; Zoltan Muzsnay
source_version: SIGMA 7 (2011), article 114, published version of record; official EMIS Brno native/PDF bytes exactly match historical publisher pins; acquired 2026-10-03
difficulty_reason: A curvature compatibility condition is not sufficient for jet prolongation merely because it is necessary for an actual solution. The authors compute the prolonged projective-metrizability symbol and its cokernel, construct five explicit Spencer obstruction components, and use a vertical-structure preserving connection to identify their values. Four components cancel by Frolicher-Nijenhuis commutators while the remaining tau4 component is exactly the nonlinear-connection curvature obstruction, giving both directions of the finite-order lift criterion.

Independent held quasi-regular-basis argument is not used. Corrected editor difficulty text names the remaining tau4 curvature component; all original authored body bytes retained. counted_scope: One proposed counted original result: complete Theorem 4.3, the pointwise first-order-to-second-order formal jet lifting equivalence with d_R theta=0. All original manifold/form/spray hypotheses and both directions are retained, without adding a dimension restriction. The full source-local calculus, operator symbols, and kernel-dimension computations needed by the cokernel and five explicit obstruction maps are included. The separate quasi-regular-basis argument for Theorem4.2 and analytic existence consequences remain held and are not invoked as a proof of this finite-order result.
historical_catalog_title: For a spray on a smooth real manifold of dimension at least three, a first-order formal projective-metrizability jet lifts to second order exactly when its nonlinear-connection curvature obstruction vanishes
current_target_scope: Full original Theorem4.3, without inventing a dimension restriction, pointwise finite first-to-second formal jet lifting iff d_R theta=0. Not global involutivity, all-order formal integrability or analytic existence.
